metadata.title: Middle School A+++ Art History — 13-Week Global Visual Culture Course
research_basis: National Core Arts Standards: Visual Arts
College Board AP Art History skills adapted to middle-school level

course_goals: Develop strong visual literacy and evidence-based close looking.
Study major global artistic traditions without treating Western art as the sole center of art history.
Connect art to religion, politics, economics, technology, environment, identity, trade, migration, and social change.
Distinguish observation, interpretation, and unsupported opinion.
Recognize that artists, communities, museums, and historians can offer different perspectives.

weeks.weekly_goal: Master what is art history? through visual literacy, contextual reasoning, comparison, interpretation, and transfer.

lessons.title: What Counts as Art?
objectives: Develop middle school understanding of what counts as art?.
Use visual evidence and precise art vocabulary.
Connect artistic choices to culture, history, audience, purpose, materials, and ideas.
activities: Close-looking: observe, describe, infer, question.
Context investigation with teacher-curated museum or primary/secondary sources.
Apply the concept through analysis, comparison, research, or making.
Discuss and write an evidence-based interpretation.
Reflect, revise, and transfer the concept to an unfamiliar work.
lessons.assessment: Exit analysis, discussion, written response, sketch/studio evidence, or research note.
lessons.extension: Compare an additional work, evaluate another interpretation, or create an informed artistic response.
